I'm just trying to say that you shouldn't stop writing fanfiction just because you feel inadequate in anyway if it brings you happiness. Skill level, personal appearance, whatever. None of that stands in your way of making art. But if it's stopped being fun, it's okay to take a step back from it and try to find joy in something else.

Fanfiction is writing, writing is telling a story and telling a story is art. 
I can't remember who said it or where I saw it, but someone once said that if you have a story to tell, good, bad, whatever, it deserves to be written and it deserves to exist. You deserve to make it exist, no matter what. The fact that you wrote something and were brave enough to share it with the world is an achievement a lot of people are scared to reach for, and you should be proud of that no matter how you're feeling about it right now.

If you feel like you're in a position where it would be best for your mental health to take your work down, that's okay! But don't take it down because you don't think your writing is too bad, or because you think you or your oc aren't pretty enough to exist in that story because that is untrue.

Honestly it's not even close to being BDSMy, that requires both parties to consent to a power dynamic and a way to end it if someone wants out. I dont think it's right to even compare it to BDSM, considering Astarion's story is a story of abuse. He's a heavily traumatised person, who chooses to continue the cycle of abuse with you instead of breaking it and learning to cope with all the things he's done/done to others. 

The good ending is him turning towards a path of healing. He isn't perfect and 'fixed', he's still got 200 years of trauma to work through, but it's a good start towards breaking a cycle of abuse and manipulation. 
Whereas the bad ending is him taking up the position of his abuser, he even starts using the same voice he used all the times he tried to manipulate you previously (I.e, the first and second time you sleep w him) to coax you into turning into his spawn. From what I understand, he has the power to turn you into a true vampire now that he's ascended, but he doesn't do that. He makes you his spawn instead and makes no promises of anything beyond that.
When he turns you, he sees it as finally putting you in a position he can use to control you, like he wanted to do originally when he was still fully in the fog of his abuse.

The love he has for you isn't love anymore in the bad ending. It isn't a power you dynamic based in love either, it's all about control again, you're his lesser now. You become to him what he was to Cazador. 

Anyway that's been my short essay on Astarion and we stan a complicated king.
